namespace rest_rpc {
enum class rpc_errc : std::int8_t {
  ok = 0,
  no_such_function,
  no_such_key,
  invalid_req_type,
  function_exception,
  function_unknown_exception,
  invalid_argument,
  write_error,
  read_error,
  socket_closed,
  resolve_timeout,
  connection_timeout,
  request_timeout,
  protocol_error,
  has_response,
  duplicate_topic,
  rpc_context_init_failed,
};
} // namespace rest_rpc
objects.description: Strongly-typed error code enumeration for the rest_rpc library, stored as int8_t. Values map to specific RPC/client errors and are used with std::error_code via the custom error_category provided in this header.

Custom std::error_category implementation for mapping rest_rpc::rpc_errc values to category name and human-readable messages. Typically used to create std::error_code instances along with make_error_code(rpc_errc). Singleton access is provided via rest_rpc::category().

A no-op logger type in the rest_rpc namespace. Any streamed input via operator<< is ignored, enabling logging call sites to compile away without side effects. Useful as a sink in release builds. No state and no resources; trivially constructible/destructible.

Logger that streams values to std::cout using operator<<. On destruction, it emits a trailing newline to std::cout. Designed for temporary rvalue usage via macros to build a single log line across chained << operations.

Logger that streams values to std::cerr using operator<<. On destruction, it emits a trailing newline to std::cerr. Intended for temporary rvalue instances created by macros to compose a single log message via operator<< chaining.

A constexpr MD5 hashing helper struct implementing a compile-time friendly subset of MD5. Provides internal data structures, constants, and functions to process a message and compute a 32-bit hash. Intended for use where MD5 needs to be evaluated at compile time.
Internal 128-bit state container for the MD5 computation, holding the four 32-bit words a, b, c, d used across rounds.

functions.name: rest_rpc::rpc_error_category::name
functions.description: Returns the name of the error category as a C string literal. Intended for use with std::error_code and std::error_category interfaces to identify this category ("rest_rpc_error"). No state is accessed and the function is noexcept.
requirements: No preconditions on the object state; may be called at any time on a valid rest_rpc::rpc_error_category instance.
The returned pointer is a string literal and must not be freed or modified.

functions.name: rest_rpc::rpc_error_category::message
functions.description: Maps an integer error value (expected to be a rest_rpc::rpc_errc value) to a human-readable message string. Used by std::error_code to render error messages for this category. If ev does not correspond to a known rest_rpc::rpc_errc, returns "unknown error".
requirements: ev should correspond to a value of rest_rpc::rpc_errc to get a defined message; other values yield "unknown error".
No other preconditions; callable on any valid rest_rpc::rpc_error_category instance.

functions.name: rest_rpc::category
functions.description: Returns a reference to the singleton instance of the rest_rpc error category. Use this when constructing std::error_code objects for rest_rpc::rpc_errc values or when associating errors with this category.
requirements: The returned reference refers to a function-local static with static storage duration; do not attempt to delete or take ownership.
Thread-safe initialization is guaranteed in C++11 and later.

functions.name: rest_rpc::make_error_code
functions.description: Constructs a std::error_code from a rest_rpc::rpc_errc value using the rest_rpc error category. Intended to integrate rpc_errc with standard error handling.
requirements: Parameter e may be any enumerator of rest_rpc::rpc_errc.
The resulting std::error_code uses rest_rpc::category() as its category.

functions.name: rest_rpc::operator==
functions.signature: bool rest_rpc::operator==(const std::error_code& code, rest_rpc::rpc_errc ec)
functions.description: Compares a std::error_code to a rest_rpc::rpc_errc value by checking if code.value() equals the integral value of ec. Note: this comparison ignores the error category, which may be surprising if code carries a different category.
requirements: No preconditions on code; it may originate from any category.
Be aware that the comparison only checks the numeric value and ignores code.category().

functions.name: rest_rpc::null_logger_t::operator<<
functions.signature:
template <typename T>
const rest_rpc::null_logger_t& rest_rpc::null_logger_t::operator<<(T&&) const;
functions.description: No-op stream-insertion operator for the null logger. Accepts any value and returns the same logger instance without producing output or side effects. Intended to allow logging expressions to compile while discarding their content (e.g., in release builds or when a log level is disabled). Usage: REST_LOG_WARNING << "message"; when REST_LOG_WARNING resolves to NULL_LOGGER, the chain compiles but does nothing.
requirements: Accepts any type T; there is no requirement that T be stream-insertable.
No side effects; safe to call with any argument, including temporaries and moved-from objects.
Logger object must be a valid instance (e.g., a temporary created by macros or a persistent object).

functions.name: rest_rpc::cout_logger_t::operator<<
functions.signature:
template <typename T>
const rest_rpc::cout_logger_t& rest_rpc::cout_logger_t::operator<<(T&& t) const;
functions.description: Stream-insertion operator that forwards the provided value to std::cout, enabling chaining of log parts. Returns the same logger instance to allow multiple << operations in a single expression. Typically used via macros that create a temporary cout_logger_t so that a newline is emitted upon destruction.
requirements: The expression (std::cout << t) must be well-formed; i.e., T must be stream-insertable into std::ostream.
std::cout must be in a usable state; I/O failures will propagate via std::ostream state (no exceptions are specified here).
The logger object must remain alive for the duration of the chained insertions in the expression.

functions.name: rest_rpc::cout_logger_t::~cout_logger_t
functions.description: Destructor that writes a newline (std::endl) to std::cout, typically finalizing a log line when a temporary logger goes out of scope. Used implicitly at the end of a logging expression to terminate the line and flush the stream.
requirements: std::cout must be in a usable state; destructor performs std::cout << std::endl.
Destruction timing follows normal C++ lifetime rules; when used as a temporary, the newline is emitted at the end of the full expression.

functions.name: rest_rpc::cerr_logger_t::operator<<
functions.signature:
template <typename T>
const rest_rpc::cerr_logger_t& rest_rpc::cerr_logger_t::operator<<(T&& t) const;
functions.description: Stream-insertion operator that forwards the provided value to std::cerr, enabling chaining of log parts. Returns the same logger instance to allow multiple << operations. Typically used via macros that create a temporary cerr_logger_t so that a newline is emitted upon destruction.
requirements: The expression (std::cerr << t) must be well-formed; i.e., T must be stream-insertable into std::ostream.
std::cerr must be in a usable state; I/O failures will propagate via std::ostream state (no exceptions are specified here).
The logger object must remain alive for the duration of the chained insertions in the expression.

functions.name: rest_rpc::cerr_logger_t::~cerr_logger_t
functions.description: Destructor that writes a newline (std::endl) to std::cerr, typically finalizing a log line when a temporary logger goes out of scope. Used implicitly at the end of a logging expression to terminate the line and flush the stream.
requirements: std::cerr must be in a usable state; destructor performs std::cerr << std::endl.
Destruction timing follows normal C++ lifetime rules; when used as a temporary, the newline is emitted at the end of the full expression.

functions.name: rest_rpc::detail::qualified_name_of_impl
functions.signature:
template <auto Func>
constexpr auto qualified_name_of_impl() noexcept
functions.description: Compile-time extraction of a function’s fully qualified name from compiler-specific pretty-function/funcsig strings. Intended to be used with a non-type template parameter representing a function (or pointer/reference to one). It normalizes names across MSVC, Clang, and GCC, removes anonymous-namespace qualifiers, and trims trailing signature/suffix text, returning the function’s qualified name as a string_view. Usage: instantiate as qualified_name_of_impl<some_function>() in a constant-evaluated context.
requirements: Func must be a valid non-type template parameter referring to a function (or function pointer/reference) that is usable in a constant expression.
Supported compilers are limited to MSVC, Clang, or GCC; other compilers will trigger a compile-time error via #error.
The extracted name format depends on the compiler’s __FUNCSIG__ (MSVC) or __PRETTY_FUNCTION__ (Clang/GCC) and may vary across compilers and versions.
Function is constexpr and noexcept; it must be usable in constant-evaluated contexts if used that way.

functions.name: rest_rpc::string_view_array_has
functions.signature:
template <size_t N>
constexpr std::string_view string_view_array_has(const std::array<std::string_view, N>& array, std::string_view value)
functions.description: Returns the first element from the provided array that is a prefix of value (i.e., where value.find(v) == 0). If no element matches, returns an empty string_view. Useful for checking whether value starts with any known prefixes. Can be evaluated at compile time when arguments are constexpr.
requirements: array must be a valid reference to an array of std::string_view values of size N.
value may be any std::string_view; no special encoding or null-termination requirements beyond std::string_view semantics.
If no prefix matches, the function returns an empty std::string_view (length 0).
The first matching element in iteration order is returned; order of array elements influences the result.
Function is constexpr; callers may use it in constant-evaluated contexts if inputs are constexpr.

functions.name: rest_rpc::get_func_name
functions.description: Returns a normalized function name for the given function non-type template parameter by obtaining its qualified name via qualified_name_of_v<func> and stripping known calling-convention prefixes (e.g., __cdecl, __stdcall) when present. Intended for compile-time retrieval of a clean function name string_view.
requirements: func must be a valid non-type template parameter referring to a function (or function pointer/reference) that is usable in a constant expression.
Relies on rest_rpc::detail::qualified_name_of_impl and the same compiler support constraints (MSVC, Clang, or GCC).

Only the specific calling convention prefixes listed in the implementation (__cdecl, __clrcall, __stdcall, __fastcall, __thiscall, __vectorcall) are stripped; other compiler- or platform-specific decorations may remain.
Function is constexpr; callers may use it in constant-evaluated contexts if the template argument resolves at compile time.

functions.name: rest_rpc::MD5::MD5Hash32
functions.signature: constexpr uint32_t rest_rpc::MD5::MD5Hash32(const char* string, uint32_t length)
functions.description: Computes a 32-bit value derived from the MD5 hash of the input buffer. It runs a constexpr implementation of MD5 over the first `length` bytes at `string` and returns the big-endian form of the MD5 A-word (i.e., a 32-bit truncation of MD5). The input is treated as raw bytes; it need not be null-terminated. Can be used at compile time when called with constant-expression arguments.
requirements: The `string` pointer must reference a readable buffer of at least `length` bytes. If `length == 0`, `string` may be null.
`length` is the exact number of bytes to hash; the data is not required to be null-terminated and any bytes after `length` are ignored.
The function accepts arbitrary binary data; no encoding assumptions are made.
To use in constant evaluation (constexpr), both arguments must be constant expressions under the compiler’s rules.
The function does not perform bounds checking or throw; callers must ensure the buffer validity to avoid undefined behavior.

data_types.description: A byte buffer carried in a std::string produced by FUZZ_PARAM_STR and treated as raw bytes. May contain any 8-bit values including null bytes, non-UTF-8 sequences, and control characters. Functions may use it as text for streaming/logging, as general string content for comparisons/prefix checks, or as binary input for hashing.

generators.generator:
import random
import struct
import itertools

def _rand_bytes(rng: random.Random, n: int) -> bytes:
    return bytes(rng.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(n))

def _biased_lengths(rng: random.Random, max_len: int):
    # Yields interesting lengths within [0, max_len]
    candidates = {0, 1, 2, 3, 15, 16, 17, 31, 32, 33, 63, 64, 65, 127, 128, 129, 255, 256, 257, 511, 512, 1023, 1024}
    for v in sorted(candidates):
        if v <= max_len:
            yield v
    # Add a few random ones
    for _ in range(8):
        yield rng.randrange(0, max_len + 1)

def _make_texty(rng: random.Random, length: int) -> bytes:
    # Construct a mixture useful for logger streaming and prefix checks.
    parts = []
    # Some readable content with spaces and punctuation
    alpha = b"abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyzABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ0123456789 _-:/\\.\n\t"
    if length <= 0:
        return b""
    # Ensure presence of hex/dec-relevant tokens and C-string edge cases
    tokens = [b"cout begin:", b"cerr begin:", b"dtor cout:", b"dtor cerr:"]
    rng.shuffle(tokens)
    while tokens and sum(len(p) for p in parts) + len(tokens[0]) <= length:
        parts.append(tokens.pop(0))
        if sum(len(p) for p in parts) < length:
            parts.append(b" ")
    # Fill remaining with readable bytes
    need = length - sum(len(p) for p in parts)
    if need > 0:
        parts.append(bytes(rng.choice(alpha) for _ in range(need)))
    return b"".join(parts)[:length]

def _make_binary(rng: random.Random, length: int) -> bytes:
    # MD5 input prefers arbitrary bytes; include NULs and high bytes.
    if length <= 0:
        return b""
    # Compose from segments: zeros, 0xFFs, incrementing, random
    segs = []
    remain = length
    patterns = [
        lambda n: b"\x00" * n,
        lambda n: b"\xff" * n,
        lambda n: bytes((i % 256) for i in range(n)),
        lambda n: _rand_bytes(rng, n),
    ]
    while remain > 0:
        take = min(remain, rng.randint(1, min(64, remain)))
        segs.append(rng.choice(patterns)(take))
        remain -= take
    return b"".join(segs)

def _encode_sections(sections):
    # Simple length-prefixed sections: [count][len][data]...
    # count: uint16, len: uint16, data bytes
    out = bytearray()
    out += struct.pack('<H', len(sections))
    for s in sections:
        out += struct.pack('<H', len(s))
        out += s
    return bytes(out)

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    # We target a single buffer consumed by FUZZ_PARAM_STR uses across stubs.
    # Build a container with multiple candidate strings; the harness can pick from them.
    # Keep total under 4096 bytes.

    sections = []

    # 1) Non-empty value for string_view_array_has with embedded prefixes
    base_len = rng.choice(list(_biased_lengths(rng, 256))) or 20
    value = _make_texty(rng, max(1, base_len))

    # Insert multiple prefixes of value to exercise matches
    prefixes = []
    for L in [0, 1, len(value)//4, len(value)//2, max(0, len(value)-1)]:
        L = max(0, min(L, len(value)))
        prefixes.append(value[:L])
    # Add a few random non-prefix strings
    for _ in range(3):
        prefixes.append(_make_texty(rng, rng.randint(0, 16)))

    # Build a section encoding for the string_view_array_has scenario
    # Layout: tag=1, then [value][N][prefix0..]
    sva_payload = bytearray()
    sva_payload += struct.pack('<H', len(value)) + value
    sva_payload += struct.pack('<H', len(prefixes))
    for p in prefixes:
        sva_payload += struct.pack('<H', len(p)) + p
    sections.append(b"\x01" + bytes(sva_payload))

    # 2) Logger-friendly text strings for cout/cerr/null logger
    for tag in (b"\x02", b"\x03", b"\x04"):
        ln = rng.choice(list(_biased_lengths(rng, 128)))
        s = _make_texty(rng, ln)
        sections.append(tag + struct.pack('<H', len(s)) + s)

    # 3) MD5 binary buffers: provide several varying sizes including 0
    for ln in itertools.islice(_biased_lengths(rng, 2048), 0, 8):
        buf = _make_binary(rng, ln)
        sections.append(b"\x05" + struct.pack('<H', len(buf)) + buf)

    # 4) Edge-case tiny strings and C-string with NULs for logger and MD5
    tiny_cases = [b"", b"\x00", b"\x00A\x00", b"hex 0xdead", b"dec 123", b"prefix"]
    for t in tiny_cases:
        sections.append(b"\x06" + struct.pack('<H', len(t)) + t)

    blob = _encode_sections(sections)
    return blob[:4096]
